analysis.investment_thesis: B.R.Goyal ticks several SMILE boxes — 270 Cr market cap, 73.6% promoter holding, 8.4x P/E and 25.6% net profit CAGR — riding India's infra capex wave. But civil construction is a working-capital-heavy, low-moat commodity business, and 2025's -36 Cr OCF plus -58 Cr FCF right after an equity raise is a yellow flag that tempers multibagger conviction.
key_strengths: Sweet-spot small-cap (270 Cr) at cheap 8.4x P/E with 73.6% promoter skin-in-game
Net profit CAGR 25.6% (8→25 Cr) with expanding op margins (7.5%→8.4%)
Balance sheet recently strengthened: equity doubled to 245 Cr, D/E just 0.31
key_risks: OCF collapsed to -36 Cr in 2025 and FCF -58 Cr — classic EPC working-capital trap
Civil construction is commoditized, margin-thin (NPM ~5%), no pricing power or moat
Revenue dipped 589→510 Cr in 2025 — lumpy order book risk typical of road/highway contractors
red_flags: Negative operating cash flow in 2025 despite record profits — earnings quality concern
Recent equity raise (likely IPO proceeds) deployed into receivables/WIP, not compounding assets yet
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a SMILE lens, B.R.Goyal has the surface markers I hunt for: small size (270 Cr), promoter at 73.6%, negligible FII presence (0.41%) meaning it's under-discovered, cheap at 8.4x P/E, and operating in the massive Indian infrastructure TAM. Profitability trajectory is genuinely encouraging — net profit has 3x'd from 8 Cr (2020) to 25 Cr (2025) at a 25.6% CAGR, ROCE of 17.9% is respectable, and debt is modest at 77 Cr against 245 Cr equity. This is the kind of under-the-radar compounder profile I scout for.

However, civil construction is a space I approach with caution. The 2025 OCF of -36 Cr and FCF of -58 Cr tell me profits are trapped in receivables and unbilled WIP — typical EPC pain. Revenue fell 13% YoY (589→510 Cr), showing execution lumpiness. The moat is weak: this is bid-based contracting against L&T, KNR, PNC, HG Infra. For a true Kedia multibagger I need a transformation catalyst — asset-light pivot, specialized vertical, or national scale-up — and I don't see that yet. At this valuation it's not expensive, but I'd wait one or two quarters to see if OCF normalizes post equity-deployment before sizing up. Score 5: interesting, cheap, watchlist material rather than conviction buy.
